items.title: Understanding Intersecting Lines
items.explanation: When two straight lines meet on a plane surface at a single point, they are said to intersect. This creates four angles around the intersection point. For example, if line l intersects line m, four angles (a, b, c, d) are formed. Adjacent angles like ∠a and ∠b form a linear pair because they add up to 180°.

items.title: Properties of Intersecting Angles
items.explanation: When two lines intersect, vertically opposite angles (like ∠b and ∠d) are always equal. Additionally, adjacent angles that form a linear pair are also always equal to each other because they both add up to 180°.

items.title: Perpendicular Lines
items.explanation: Perpendicular lines are a special case of intersecting lines where all four angles formed at the intersection are right angles (90°). This occurs when two lines meet at exactly 90 degrees, as shown in Fig. 5.4.

items.title: Parallel Lines
items.explanation: Parallel lines are a pair of lines that lie on the same plane and do not meet, no matter how far they are extended beyond their ends. Examples include opposite sides of a rectangle or the top and bottom edges of a book.
